title: How Much Fiber in Prunes? 3.4g per 5 Prunes
description: Prunes: about 3.4 g of fiber per 5 prunes (12% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in prunes?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Plums, dried (prunes), uncooked

intro: Prunes rank #8 of 15 fruits on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in prunes by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in prunes?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists plums, dried (prunes), uncooked at 7.1 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (5 prunes; 47.5 g) therefore has about 3.4 g of fiber and 114 calories. That is 12% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 13% of a 25 g day and 9% of a 38 g day.

Prunes (dried plums) are the classic food remedy for constipation, and the evidence supports it: in a randomized trial, 50 g of prunes twice a day worked at least as well as psyllium for mild to moderate constipation. They combine fiber with sorbitol, a sugar alcohol that draws water into the bowel.

sections.heading: Prunes vs prune juice
paragraphs: Prune juice keeps the sorbitol but loses most of the fiber, so it can still have a laxative effect with little fiber. Whole prunes give both.
Because of the sorbitol, a large serving of prunes can cause gas or loose stools. Start with three to five and see how you respond.

sections.heading: How prunes compare with other fruits
paragraphs: Of the 15 fruits on this site, prunes rank #8 for fiber per typical serving and #12 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 3 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [blueberries](/fiber-in-blueberries) at 3.6 g (1 cup); [orange](/fiber-in-orange) at 3.1 g (1 medium); [dried figs](/fiber-in-dried-figs) at 3.6 g (1/4 cup). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), prunes are #35 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding prunes to your day
paragraphs: Chop prunes into oatmeal, eat a few with a handful of walnuts, or simmer them into a stew with lentils.

Example: 5 prunes, 1 oz walnuts. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 5.3 g of fiber, with 3.4 g from the prunes. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of prunes?
faqs.a: 7.1 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Plums, dried (prunes), uncooked). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in prunes (1 prune)?
faqs.a: About 0.7 g, for 9.5 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: How many prunes a day for constipation?
faqs.a: One well-known trial used 50 g twice a day, roughly five or six prunes each time. Many people do well with less. Start lower, drink water, and talk to a clinician if constipation persists.
Yes, like all dried fruit they are concentrated. Five prunes have roughly 115 calories. They are a useful food, but portions matter.
